tests.name: The same checkpoint triggered twice runs once (run key = trigger · checkpoint · dataset · config)
Concurrent claims: one worker holds the lease; another can take over only after it expires
An older checkpoint replayed late never overwrites a later version
Crash after staging: nothing is visible; the restart discards staging and publishes once
Crash inside publish: the transaction rolls back; no partial insight or notification
Crash after commit or during delivery: re-trigger is a no-op and each notification is delivered exactly once
Triggers arriving in any order give the same versions, candidates and notifications
Deterministic replay: the detector replay and the runner replay are byte-identical across runs
Only notified versions create outbox rows (silent updates, Watch and merges do not)
Late-arriving rows are invisible to earlier checkpoints and visible from their ingestion run on
A corrected dataset version gets a new run key; the insight gains a version marked “data corrected”, earlier versions keep their dataset, no notification without a band rise
Insights whose evidence predates the latest dataset version are flagged stale until re-evaluated
